answer.rationale: With 14 days to expiry, no auto-renew, and the line at 94% with no buffer, a primary-vendor switch could buy unit-cost relief but raises continuity risk; renewal with the incumbent preserves delivery but fails the mandated cut unless terms move. I would verify the two negotiation memories before committing: renewal benchmarking and multi-year/volume levers are the only inherited lessons that can reduce TCO while keeping incumbent supply stable. Intended move is a guarded renewal negotiation targeting price-equivalent concessions, payment terms, rebates, volume tiers, or a short extension rather than reopening list price or changing suppliers this cycle.
